title: York man was held at gunpoint over incorrect Flock hit. Sheriff blames illegal tag cover

reading.body:
This is a false-positive failure in an automated identification system, and it occurred at the point where a machine's output was converted into police action. A license-plate reader misread one character of a plate and returned a match to a stolen vehicle. That output is a candidate match rather than an identification, and it was acted on as though it were one.

The gap sits between the alert and the enforcement. The vendor's own position is that alerts should be independently verified before enforcement, and the account does not describe that verification being completed before the man was held at gunpoint. Catching this would have taken a human confirming the plate against the vehicle and the underlying record before anyone drew a weapon.

What is not established is the cause and the judgment. The events rest on a single outlet's reporting, the sheriff's office finding that the deputy's actions were reasonable is the agency's own conclusion about its own officer, and its explanation that an illegal tinted plate cover caused the misread is the agency's account rather than an independent determination.

reports.title: York man was held at gunpoint over incorrect Flock hit. Sheriff blames illegal tag cover

summary: Steven Melvin, 42, of York County, South Carolina, was reportedly held at gunpoint for over five minutes after a Flock Safety license-plate reader misread the first letter of his plate and matched his BMW to a similar stolen vehicle. The sheriff's office later said an illegal tinted plate cover caused the malfunction and found the deputy's actions reasonable. Flock said alerts should be independently verified before enforcement.
title_en: York man was held at gunpoint over incorrect Flock hit. Sheriff blames illegal tag cover
